odia: ପେଟ କାଟ ମୁଣ୍ଡ କାଟ ଏକା କଥା
title: Cut off food, cut off life
literal_meaning: Stopping someone’s food and cutting off their head are called the same thing.
explanation: The dictionary places the saying under stopping someone’s food. Its stark comparison gives deprivation the force of a threat to life. Our reading treats that equivalence as rhetorical emphasis on food’s importance, not a clinical equation or an instruction to injure anyone. The line does not identify who withholds food or describe an actual incident.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କରିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ତୀବ୍ର ତୁଳନାଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ କରିବାକୁ ଜୀବନ ପ୍ରତି ବିପଦ ପରି ଦେଖାଏ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏହାକୁ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଉପରେ ଜୋର ବୋଲି ବୁଝେ, ଚିକିତ୍ସାଗତ ସମାନତା ବା କାହାକୁ ଆଘାତ ଦେବା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ। କିଏ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କଲା ବା ସତରେ କଣ ଘଟିଲା, କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading takes the food-deprivation warning seriously without literalizing its violence.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚନାର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦେଖେ, ହିଂସାକୁ ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ କରେନାହିଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ସମୂହ ଭୋଜନର ତାଲିକାରେ କାହାର ନାମ ଛାଡ଼ିଗଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦଳଟି ପୁଣି ଦେଖିଲା। / Organizers check that nobody has been omitted from a shared meal. This scene is invented.
cultural_context: Sense1 is distinct from eating smaller portions in later senses. No dietary, medical or financial recommendation, verified deprivation event or traditional charity rule is supplied.
